description: Draft a governance-compliant GitHub issue for HUMAN review — never submitted (AI-governance / Human-In-The-Loop contract). draft_governance_issue assembles a local Markdown draft plus a structured compliance report and validates it against the zero-dependency + reproduction policy. The server has NO network code path and NO GitHub write path: present the returned draft and compliance report to the user, then STOP — they review and submit it manually under their own GitHub identity. Engine behaviour targets 'zipnative'; wrapper behaviour targets 'zipnative-mcp'. Fully self-contained (no archive needed).

arguments.title: Expose a label-based nameEncoding input for legacy archive names
arguments.summary: Archives written by older Japanese and Russian tools store Shift-JIS or CP866 names without the UTF-8 flag; list_zip_entries shows them as CP437 mojibake. zipnative 1.1.0 can decode them (nameDecoder), but zipnative-mcp deliberately exposes no decoder. A closed enum of TextDecoder labels would reach the feature without accepting code from the caller.

reproduction.command: list_zip_entries on an archive whose names are Shift-JIS bytes without flag bit 11
reproduction.result: every name is decoded as CP437 (nameEncoding: 'cp437'); rawNameHex shows the original Shift-JIS bytes

arguments.expectedBehavior: An optional nameEncoding input (a closed enum such as 'shift_jis' | 'cp866' | 'windows-1251') decodes the names before path sanitisation; the default stays CP437.
arguments.actualBehavior: The names cannot be decoded by any tool input.
